expectedRelation: ARTIFICIAL_OR_FICTIONAL_SOLID_SHELL, DECLARED_ARTIFICIAL_SOLID_SURFACE, and DECLARED_ARTIFICIAL_LAYER_STACK are eligible only when an explicit artificial-solid-shell exception permission and declared structure are both present.
weightRationale: This is a hard product-scope gate, not probabilistic scientific evidence.
exceptions: Explicit permission alone does not invent an unprovided artificial layer stack.

expectedRelation: Radius-density combinations compatible with rocky solid-planet models may support ROCKY_TERRESTRIAL or ROCKY_SUPER_EARTH candidates and a DIFFERENTIATED_METAL_SILICATE layer-stack candidate.
weightRationale: Independent rocky-interior and differentiation models support the broad stack while not fixing detailed composition.
exceptions: Low-density or volatile-rich cases retain non-rocky alternatives.
Mass and radius alone do not prove a unique core fraction.

expectedRelation: Water-rich solid bodies may preserve high-pressure-ice-bearing alternatives rather than assuming direct liquid-water contact with rock.
weightRationale: Multiple water-world structure models predict pressure-dependent water phases, but exact phase boundaries remain downstream.
exceptions: Exact phase boundaries require later thermodynamic modeling.
Low water inventory may remove the high-pressure-ice alternative.

expectedRelation: Water-rich, sufficiently cold solid bodies with compatible internal heat may support ICE_SHELL_OCEAN_BODY, ICE_SHELL_SURFACE, and ICE_SHELL_LIQUID_LAYER_ROCKY_INTERIOR candidates.
weightRationale: Independent ice-covered ocean-world models support the broad candidate architecture while retaining uncertainty in layer thickness and chemistry.
exceptions: An ice shell does not guarantee a liquid layer.
Exact shell and ocean thickness remain unresolved.

expectedRelation: Radius and density can support broad solid-body family candidates such as rocky, rock-ice, or water-rich solids, but are not sufficient to resolve detailed composition.
weightRationale: Mass-radius models provide broad physical compatibility bounds and explicit composition degeneracy.
exceptions: Atmospheric envelopes can mimic lower-density solid compositions.

expectedRelation: When atmospheric-envelope state is not independently constrained, water-rich solid and rocky-plus-envelope explanations remain degenerate and the premise must preserve alternatives or remain PARTIAL.
weightRationale: The rule prevents false uniqueness from bulk density and radius alone.
exceptions: Independent atmospheric constraints may reduce ambiguity.

expectedRelation: Premise rules may resolve only body class, broad layer stack, and broad surface medium; they may not infer tectonic regime, impacts, plates, continents, basins, landforms, terrain, climate results, hydrology, biomes, materials, or rendering.
weightRationale: This is a hard causal-scope firewall.

expectedRelation: PARTIALLY_DIFFERENTIATED_ROCKY may be preserved as an alternative when broad inputs do not justify a fully differentiated or fully mixed stack, but this rule cannot support COMPLETE resolution.
weightRationale: The available W1-02A inputs do not encode formation and thermal history with enough fidelity for a unique partial-differentiation decision.
exceptions: No COMPLETE result may rely on this rule.
Thermal history is underconstrained at premise stage.

expectedRelation: Low-density, volatile-rich solid inputs may support ROCK_ICE_MIXED_SOLID_BODY with UNDIFFERENTIATED_ROCK_ICE_MIXTURE and DIFFERENTIATED_ROCK_ICE alternatives rather than forcing a clean shell-over-core model.
weightRationale: Solid mass-radius models and high-pressure ice-rock interaction models independently support broad rock-ice alternatives.
exceptions: High-pressure miscibility results do not apply uniformly across all masses.
Mass-radius degeneracy requires multiple candidates when envelopes are unconstrained.

expectedRelation: Stars, stellar remnants, brown dwarfs, gas giants without a coherent artificial shell, and fluid-only bodies without a coherent shell are BLOCKED from the WorldWright solid-surface route.
weightRationale: This is a hard supported-route boundary rather than a claim that such bodies are scientifically impossible.
exceptions: A declared artificial solid shell is handled by the separate exception rule.

expectedRelation: Water- or volatile-rich solid bodies under sufficiently strong irradiation or declared greenhouse constraints may preserve VOLATILE_PRESSURE_SOLID_BODY, VOLATILE_MODIFIED_SOLID_SURFACE, and VOLATILE_PRESSURE_OVER_SOLID_INTERIOR alternatives.
weightRationale: Water-world and irradiated-water-rich models support a pressure-dominated volatile layer while exact climate thresholds remain unresolved.
exceptions: Declared albedo and greenhouse values are constraints, not a completed climate model.
